evals.name: word-frequency-cli-from-an-empty-directory
evals.prompt: Build this unattended, start to finish, and stop at a merge request I can review: a command-line tool that prints the N most frequent words in a text file, ignoring case and punctuation.
evals.expected_output: A new repository with numbered requirements covered by stories, a design that matches the code, every decision taken on the user's behalf listed once as Proposed with alternatives and reasons, the tool built test first with a make check that really runs the tests, correct word handling for apostrophes, hyphens, case, decomposed accents and scripts with combining marks, deterministic ties, clean errors for bad arguments and undecodable input, a README example that matches the tool, a prepared merge request description, and the exact push command given but not run.
expectations: A git repository exists with a Makefile whose make check runs the tool's tests: it passes on the committed tree when the grader runs it, and it fails when the grader makes one test assert something false
Numbered, testable requirement statements taken from the request exist, and every one is covered by at least one story or task in a backlog

A design description (a design document, or a design section of the README or merge request description) states the tool as it was built (its modules or functions, the word rule and the output format), and nothing in it contradicts the code

Every decision the run took on the user's behalf (at least language, argument form, output format, the word rule and tie ordering) is listed in one place for review, each with the alternatives considered and a reason, marked Proposed or awaiting review; none says Accepted and none names a person as having decided

On the grader's UTF-8 file containing "The cat's toy. THE CAT, the dog-dog; Cafe cafe CAFE and café Café", then café written decomposed (e followed by U+0301), then the line "नमस्ते दुनिया नमस्ते": the tool counts THE/The/the together, counts the two composed café forms and the decomposed one as one word with count 3 printed as café (an accent is neither case nor punctuation, so cafe stays its own word with count 3), prints नमस्ते whole with count 2 and दुनिया whole (never fragments split at a vowel sign or virama), and treats the apostrophe and the hyphen the way its recorded word-rule decision says

Words with equal counts are printed in a deterministic order that the documentation states, a test pins that order, and an N larger than the number of distinct words prints every word once without an error

A missing input file, a non-numeric N and an N of zero or less each produce an error on stderr that names the bad value or file and a non-zero exit status, with no Python traceback (or the equivalent stack dump in another language), and what stderr shows matches what the run's own PRD, README or merge request promises (a promised one-line error is one line, not an argument library's usage block plus the error)

On a file that is not valid UTF-8 (the grader writes the bytes of "caf" followed by 0xE9 and " ok ok"), the tool either exits non-zero with a one-line error naming the file, or counts with a replacement rule its documentation states; it never prints a traceback or stack dump

The work is committed on a branch that is not main, master or develop, the branch has no upstream, and the user is given the exact command to push that branch (in the final message or the merge request description) without it having been run

A merge request description exists in the working tree (committed, or in an ignored scratch folder such as .scratch/; a file inside .git does not count) that summarises the change, says how it was verified, and lists the decisions awaiting review

The README's usage example is true: the grader runs the documented command on an input like the documented one, and the output's shape (one line per word, the order, where the count sits and what separates it) is what the README shows

evals.name: add-search-to-an-existing-notes-cli
evals.prompt: Take this to a merge request without asking me anything: add a search command to the notes tool that lists the notes containing a word, case-insensitive.
evals.expected_output: The existing notes-cli repository gains a search command built test first on a branch that reads notes the way list does (through store.notes(), so 0.1 bare-string entries are found and numbered as list numbers them), follows docs/CONVENTIONS.md for empty results, usage errors, output shape, read-only behaviour and an unreadable store (exit 1, no traceback) while reporting that list itself breaks that last rule, matches literally with full Unicode case folding, is proportional to the request, records decisions as Proposed with conventions cited rather than re-decided, passes make check, and ends at a prepared merge request with the push command given, not run.
expectations: After adding "buy milk", "Milk the cow" and "call mum" with python -m notes add, python -m notes search MILK prints exactly the first two notes, in the same `<id>: <text>` shape and stored order as list, and whether a partial-word match counts (substring or whole word) is stated as a decision for review

Following docs/CONVENTIONS.md and the existing commands: search for a word no note contains prints nothing on stdout and exits 0; search with no word, an empty word or two words prints the shared usage line to stderr and exits 2; run in a directory with no notes.json it does not create one, and after a search an existing notes.json is byte-identical

With the grader's notes.json set to ["Milk run", {"id": 2, "text": "call mum"}] (a note stored by version 0.1 as a bare string, which list shows as `1: Milk run`), search milk prints exactly `1: Milk run` and exits 0, with no traceback

With a notes.json that is not valid JSON, search prints a message on stderr, exits 1 and shows no traceback, as docs/CONVENTIONS.md requires for a store that cannot be read; and the user is told (in the merge request or the final message) that list does not follow this rule today, whether the run left list alone or also changed it (a change to list is disclosed as a behaviour change)

search matches the user's word as literal text with Unicode case folding: after adding "learn c++ today", "axb" and "Grüße aus der Straße", search c++ lists the first, search a.b lists nothing, and search STRASSE lists the third

On a valid store, python -m notes add and python -m notes list behave exactly as before the change; the tests that were in tests/test_store.py are unchanged and pass (new tests may be added anywhere), and make check passes when the grader runs it

The change is proportional to the request: outside notes/, tests/ and the README, the branch adds only documents written for this change (requirements, design, decisions, test cases, merge request text, a run report), which together add no more than about 400 lines and none of which describes architecture, deployment or components the change does not touch (no C4 set, tenets, repository plan or rendered diagrams); no CI pipeline, git hooks, editor or agent configuration, templates or dependency files are added, and the Makefile's check target runs the same tests as before (a one-line addition that only records a pass is acceptable)

Any requirements, stories or design written are scoped to search and ask for nothing the request did not mention; an improvement the run noticed outside that scope is reported as a suggestion, not built

Every decision taken on the user's behalf is listed in one document or one section for review with its alternatives and a reason, marked Proposed or awaiting review; none is recorded as Accepted or attributed to a person, and a choice docs/CONVENTIONS.md already settles (empty result, usage errors, output shape, read-only) is cited as settled, not re-decided with invented alternatives

The work is committed on a branch that is not main, the branch has no upstream, nothing the run wrote is left modified or untracked outside ignored folders, and the user is given the exact command to push that branch (in the final message or the merge request description) without it having been run

A merge request description exists in the working tree (committed, or in an ignored scratch folder such as .scratch/) that summarises the change, says how it was verified and lists the decisions awaiting review
